Costs incurred by ServCo and by other NGUSA subsidiaries in providing services to NGUSA client 
companies (Client Companies), including the Company, are set forth in the service agreements and its Cost 
Allocation Manual (Revised April 2017) (CAM) and include, but are not limited to, labor and related 
overhead costs (e.g., salaries of officers and other employees, employee welfare expenses such as social 
security taxes, life insurance, pensions, post-retirement benefits other than pension, medical, dental and other 
welfare expenses), training costs, facilities costs, information technology costs, and costs related to vendor 
and other contract services. The organization, conduct of business and method of cost allocation are designed 
to result in the performance of services and the provision of goods economically and efficiently for the benefit 
of the Client Companies at cost, fairly and equitably allocated among such companies. 
 
The purpose of the CAM is to serve as a guide as to the manner in which costs should be charged to the Client 
Companies by the company incurring the cost. The prevailing premise of these cost allocation guidelines is 
that allocation methods should not result in subsidization of non-regulated services or products by regulated 
entities or subsidization of services or products from one regulated entity to another. 
 
The provision of administrative services to the Client Companies by ServCo is specified in service 
agreements filed with the respective utility regulatory commissions. 
 
Principles of cost allocation 
The following principles guide the allocation of costs of products or services provided by Servco and other 
operating subsidiaries to the Client Companies. 
 
 Direct charging or direct assignment is the preferred allocation methodology and is used if the cost of 
providing a product or service can be identified with the Client Companies receiving the benefit of that 
product or service. Direct charging should only be used if the cost of providing a product or service to an 
individual Client Company can be isolated and reported separately from costs to provide other products 
or services and from costs to provide the same product and service to other Client Companies. 
 
 The costs of products and services that cannot be direct charged should be allocated based on cost 
causative allocation bases representative of the underlying cost drivers of that product or service. 
 
 The cost allocation methodology should be comprehensive, transparent, stable and administratively 
 
manageable and cost effective. 
 
 The calculation of the cost allocation bases should be supported by a clearly defined methodology, model 
and supporting policy and procedure documentation. 
 
 The cost allocation methodology should accommodate changes in the size of the allocation bases from 
period to period based on changes in the underlying cost drivers; the allocation bases should not vary 
significantly from period to period for uncontrollable factors not related to the underlying cost drivers. 
 
 The calculation of the allocation bases should be updated at least annually and more frequently if needed 
to reflect significant events (e.g., the sale of a significant affiliate). 
 
Costs are defined among the following four categories for purposes of allocating the costs of products and 
services to the Client Companies. This hierarchy represents the order of methodologies used when 
allocating costs. These four cost categories are: 
 
 Directly Assignable – Expenses incurred for activities and services exclusively for the benefit of a 
Client Company. 
 
 Directly Attributable – Expenses incurred for activities and services that benefit more than one Client 
Company and which can be allocated based on direct measures of cost causation; for example, number of 
employees or number of customers. 
 
Exhibit______(RRP-2)
Schedule 2
Page 45 of 88


--- Page 275 ---
 
 
 
 Indirectly Attributable – Expenses incurred as a “cost of doing business” that do not relate to the 
provision of specific products and services. The costs typically benefit all entities within the corporate 
umbrella. Examples include governance costs, Corporate Secretary costs, and investor relations costs. 
These costs are typically allocated based on a general measure of cost causation, commonly referred to as 
the general allocator. Costs that cannot be directly identified with the provision of a particular product or 
service. This includes but is not limited to governance costs, insurance, and taxes as well the cost of 
services supporting ServCo such as ServCo accounting and recruiting for ServCo positions. The general 
allocator is the ratio of net plant, net margins and net operations and maintenance expenses, equally 
weighted. 
 
 Unattributable – Expenses incurred for activities or services that have been determined as not appropriate 
for apportionment to the Client Companies. These costs relate primarily to activities such as corporate 
diversification, political or philanthropic endeavors and, as such, are charged directly to the parent 
company, NGUSA. 
 
To apply these principles, ServCo and the Client Companies accumulate costs in system orders. The order 
design acts as the primary cost control element from which costs are billed to affiliates. For each order, an 
order design documents a description of the order’s use and purpose, the activities associated with that 
particular order, and justification for the allocation methodology to be used for allocating the costs 
accumulated in the order. Only one allocation methodology can be used for each order. 
 
Subsidiaries charge no more than actual costs for services provided to the Company and other regulated 
affiliates. 
 
The monthly settlements process includes only the costs accumulated in the open orders. There is no markup 
or profit included in allocations to the regulated affiliates. The allocations are based on the methodologies 
designated and described above. Accordingly, the unit cost (price) charged to these affiliates, including the 
Company, is intended to reasonably approximate the actual costs of providing such services. 
 
Section 7 of the CAM lists those services provided by ServCo and the Client Companies to whom these 
services are provided. These services are provided in accordance with the service agreements filed with the 
respective utility regulatory commissions.

Supplementary information to the Summary of Costs – NMPC 
 
The total amounts recorded by the Company for the twelve-month period ended December 31, 2019 in general ledger accounts representing operating 
expenses are summarized in the table below. The total ledger cost data (A) is the total of transactions recorded in the Company’s general ledger that relate 
to operating costs considered for recovery in customer rates. 
 
We have then subtracted items in the second column (B) costs incurred for energy efficiency programs and fleet, and accounting entries related to the 
accrual or deferral of regulatory accounting mechanisms, leaving the third column to show costs that the Finance Team selected and included in its 
examination (refer to the Notes to the Summary of Costs for more details on the method of selection). Column C, and the immediately preceding columns 
(d-h), include amounts cross-referenced to the Summary of Costs.

Supplementary information to the Summary of Costs - Service Company 
 
The total amounts recorded by the Company for the twelve-month period ended December 31, 2019 in general ledger accounts representing operating 
expenses are summarized in the table below. The total ledger cost data (A) is the total of transactions recorded in the Company’s general ledger that relate 
to operating costs considered for recovery in customer rates. 
 
We have then subtracted items in the second column (B) costs incurred for energy efficiency programs and fleet, and accounting entries related to the 
accrual or deferral of regulatory accounting mechanisms, leaving the third column to show costs that the Finance Team selected and included in its 
examination (refer to the Notes to the Summary of Costs for more details on the method of selection). Column C, and the immediately preceding columns 
(d-h), include amounts cross-referenced to the Summary of Costs.

Enclosed is the fiscal year 2020 ASC 712 expense valuation for Niagara Mohawk. The valuation is 
based on January 1, 2019 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.40 percent discount rate 
assumption, the incremental operating income for the period April 1, 2019 through March 31, 2020 is 
$1.6 million. 
Fiscal Year 2020 Valuation Results 
The plan’s overall experience in fiscal year 2020 was more favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, 
the projected liability at year-end was $0.8 million lower than expected. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
▪
Elimination of excise tax;
▪
Lower income benefits; and
▪
Slightly smaller active population; offset by
▪
A change in discount rate from 3.65% to 3.40%;
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income), as well as a summary of the assumptions and benefit 
provisions used in the valuation.

Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2020. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein. 
In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
the advice and interpretations of National Grid’s auditors. 
The actuarial assumptions and methods used in this valuation are described in the ASC 712 
Assumptions and Methods section. National Grid selected the economic, demographic, and health 
care claims cost assumptions and prescribed them for use for purposes of compliance with ASC 712-
10. Aon provided guidance with respect to these assumptions, and it is our belief that they represent
reasonable expectations of anticipated plan experience. The actuarial cost method is prescribed by
ASC 712-10.

ASC 712 Assumptions and Methods 
Cost of Medical Coverage 
The medical claims costs reflect the expected impact of the Health 
Care reform, including eligibility expansion to include dependent 
children up to age 26, elimination of lifetime maximums, and 100% in-
network preventive care coverage.  
The “Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020” signed into law 
on December 20, 2019, included a permanent repeal of the excise tax 
on high-cost plans originally imposed by the Affordable Care Act in 
2010.  As a result, there is no impact from the excise tax included in 
the valuation. 
Disabled participants are assumed to generate medical costs which 
vary with duration from disability.

National Grid USA 
Niagara Mohawk—Union 
Plan Provisions 
Eligibility for Participation 
All Niagara Mohawk Local 97 employees 
Eligibility for Benefits 
All disabled participants 
Benefits 
LTD Elimination Period  
27 weeks 
LTD Income Replacement 
Unreduced Niagara Mohawk Pension Plan transition group 
formula (regardless of whether or not participant is actually in 
the transition group. 
LTD Medical Benefits 
Active medical benefits provided to the disabled individual and 
his or her dependents 
LTD Life Insurance 
Considered immaterial and not included in the valuation 
Workers’ Compensation Medical 
Benefits  
Active medical benefits provided to the disabled individual’s 
dependents only. Employee benefits assumed to be covered by 
Workers’ Compensation program. 
Workers’ Compensation Life Insurance 
Coverage continues at the same level as while an active 
employee  
Duration of Benefits  
LTD Medical and Life Insurance 
Benefits 
Those with less than 60 points (i.e. age plus service) at time of 
disability get coverage for two years only. Those with 60 points 
or more are valued under ASC 715. 
LTD Income Replacement Benefits 
Those with less than 60 points (i.e. age plus service) at time of 
disability get coverage for two years only. Those with 60 points 
or more get coverage until the earlier of death, recovery or 
age 65. 
Workers’ Compensation 
Coverage continues until the earlier of death, recovery, age 65, 
or 12 months from the valuation date

Subject: April 1, 2019 to March 31, 2020 ASC 712 Expense Results—New England 
Enclosed is the fiscal year 2020 ASC 712 expense valuation for New England. The valuation is based 
on January 1, 2019 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.40 percent discount rate 
assumption, the incremental operating expense for the period April 1, 2019 through March 31, 2020 
is $0.6 million. 
Fiscal Year 2020 Valuation Results 
The plan’s overall experience in fiscal year 2020 was more favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, 
the projected liability at year-end was $0.4 million lower than expected. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
▪
Elimination of excise tax
▪
Fewer participants with income replacement benefits; offset by
▪
Larger active population;
▪
Higher medical costs; and
▪
A change in discount rate from 3.65% to 3.40%.
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income) by company, as well as a summary of the assumptions 
and benefit provisions used in the valuation. 
Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2020. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein.

Cost of Medical Coverage 
The medical claims costs reflect the expected impact of the Health 
Care reform, including eligibility expansion to include dependent 
children up to age 26, elimination of lifetime maximums, and 100% in-
network preventive care coverage.  
 
The “Further Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2020” signed into law 
on December 20, 2019, included a permanent repeal of the excise tax 
on high-cost plans originally imposed by the Affordable Care Act in 
2010.  As a result, there is no impact from the excise tax included in 
the valuation. 
 
Disabled participants are assumed to generate medical costs which 
vary with duration from disability:

Dear Chris, 
Subject: April 1, 2019 to March 31, 2020 ASC 712 Expense Results—KeySpan 
Enclosed is the fiscal year 2020 ASC 712 expense valuation for KeySpan. The valuation is based on 
January 1, 2019 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.40 percent discount rate assumption, 
the incremental operating income for the period April 1, 2019 through March 31, 2020 is $0.5 million. 
Fiscal Year 2020 Valuation Results 
The plan’s overall experience in fiscal year 2020 was less favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, the 
projected liability at year-end was $1.1 million higher than expected. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
▪ 
A change in discount rate from 3.65% to 3.40% 
▪ 
Unfavorable claims experience for union plans 
▪ 
More LTD claimants; offset by 
▪ 
Favorable claims experience for non-union plans 
▪ 
Removal of the adjustment for the excise tax 
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income) by business unit, as well as a summary of the 
assumptions and benefit provisions used in the valuation. 
Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2020. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein.

In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
the advice and interpretations of National Grid’s auditors. 
The actuarial assumptions and methods used in this valuation are described in the ASC 712 
Assumptions and Methods section. National Grid selected the economic, demographic, and health 
care claims cost assumptions and prescribed them for use for purposes of compliance with ASC 712-
10. Aon provided guidance with respect to these assumptions, and it is our belief that they represent 
reasonable expectations of anticipated plan experience. The actuarial cost method is prescribed by 
ASC 712-10.

NOTES
Notes on Property/Terrorism/Business Interruption Charges to NMP and LIPA
1. NM Properties (NMP) is charged a share of the Property & Terrorism premiums for its coverage under these policies.
2. LIPA is charged a share of the Property, Terrorism & Business Interruption premiums for its lease of space at several NG facilities.
1. Insurance premiums are allocated using the SAP allocation code that most closely mirrors the underlying exposures that are being insured. If an appropriate SAP allocation code is not available, the insurance premiums are allocated manually.
2. For example, the Workers Compensation, Fidelity Bond (Crime), Employment Practices Liability, and Fiduciary insurance policies have a common risk exposure – the number of employees. An all-company SAP allocation code, which is based on the number of employees, is used to allocate the
premiums to all companies covered under these policies.
3. The Property and Property Terrorism insurance premiums are based on the replacement value of the property insured and associated prior loss history. There is no predefined SAP allocation code that fits this risk exposure profile. Therefore, the insurance premiums are manually allocated to all
companies covered under these policies based on insurable values and loss history.
3. Property valuation methodology changed from 80% value/20% loss history for 2018-2019 renewal to 100% value/00% loss history for 2019-2020 renewal. This explains the substantial allocation increase for electric segment.
4. For forecast for FY22 - FY24, tailored % increase as applied rather than 2% inflation index cross the board. Given the hardening state of the insurance market and the feedback received from insurers, the rate increase will be more than 2%. Rate increase will be varied but some lines will have

701 Use remote sensors to optimize PM costs
IL5 (Realised)
37
0
0
37
Partial
Electric - Distribution
NIMOD
Install sensors just outside substations at feeder heads to reduce the need to 
conduct manual operations. All tracking will be based on planned sensor 
installations in NY and NE over the next 3 fiscal years on non EMS stations at 
the feeder head. Manual operations analyzed include TOA based feeder head 
load readings, readings of analog station load to obtain summer peak load 
readings or for regular V&O inspections, and false positive station outages due 
to single phase outages. To measure reduced OPEX it will be assumed that 
sensors will make the previously defined manual operation unnecessary; the 
calculation will be done using NY and NE data sets (where available and 
relevant) to produce system averages of number of hours spent per year per 
feeder on each operation, which will in turn inform an approximate amount of 
OPEX that can potentially be avoided (on a per sensor basis).

existing Webex training capabilities to offer one day of safety and regulatory 
training remotely to all locations as part of Annual Expert Training (AET).

15500 PiPro Data Analysis Efficiency
IL5 (Realised)
45
0
0
45
Yes - C
Electric - Distribution
NIMOD
PiPro is a software analysis tool (developed in python by DPAM) designed to 
automate the analysis of load readings out of Pi. Specifically, the tool 
automates the 'scrubbing' of the loading data, meaning it removes anomalies in 
the data (such as switching peaks and minimums, meter failure, etc.). This is 
normally manually performed by planning engineers, so the implementation of 
this tool is anticipated to deliver savings in terms of employee hours. Some 
assumptions are being made for the sake of forecasting efficiencies and savings 
around management hourly wages, and time required to perform data analysis 
tasks.
